verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.1:2: "Gathering, I will gather all things from the face of the earth," says the Lord,
verses.1:3: "gathering man and beast, gathering the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea; and there will be ruins of the wicked, and I will destroy mankind from the face of the earth," says the Lord.
verses.1:4: "And I will stretch out My hand over Judah and over all who inhabit Jerusalem, and I will destroy from this place the remnant of Baal and the names of the temple keepers along with the priests,
verses.1:5: and those who worship the host of heaven on the rooftops, and who worship and swear by the Lord, and swear by Milcom,
verses.1:6: and those who turn away from behind the back of the Lord, and who have not sought the Lord nor searched for Him."
verses.1:7: Be silent before the face of the Lord God, for the day of the Lord is near; for the Lord has prepared a sacrifice; He has consecrated His invited ones.
verses.1:8: "And it will happen on the day of the Lord's sacrifice: I will punish the princes and the sons of the king and all who are clothed in foreign attire,
verses.1:9: and I will punish everyone who arrogantly steps over the threshold on that day, those who fill the house of the Lord their God with iniquity and deceit."
verses.1:10: "And on that day," says the Lord, "there will be the sound of an outcry from the Fish Gate, and wailing from the Second, and a great shattering from the hills.
verses.1:11: Wail, inhabitants of the Mortar: all the people of Canaan have fallen silent; all who are wrapped in silver have perished.
verses.1:12: And it will happen at that time: I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men fixed in their dregs, who say in their hearts, 'The Lord will not do good, and He will not do evil.'
verses.1:13: And their strength will become plunder, and their houses a wasteland; and they will build houses and not inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards and not drink their wine."
verses.1:14: Near is the great day of the Lord; it is near and exceedingly swift. The sound of the day of the Lord is bitter; there the mighty man will be distressed.
verses.1:15: That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and anguish, a day of disaster and misery, a day of darkness and thick gloom, a day of cloud and whirlwind,
verses.1:16: a day of trumpet and blast against the fortified cities and against the high corners.
verses.1:17: "And I will distress people, and they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord; and their blood will be poured out like soil, and their bodies like dung."
verses.1:18: Even their silver and their gold will not be able to deliver them on the day of the Lord's wrath; in the fire of His zeal the whole earth will be devoured, for He will make a complete end with haste of all who inhabit the earth.
verses.2:2: before the decree brings forth the day that passes like dust, before the wrath of the Lord's fury comes upon you, before the day of the Lord's indignation comes upon you.
verses.2:3: Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth, who have carried out His judgment; seek what is just, seek what is meek, if somehow you may be hidden on the day of the Lord's fury.
verses.2:4: For Gaza will be destroyed, and Ashkelon will be a wasteland; they will drive out Ashdod at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.
verses.2:5: Woe to you who inhabit the strip by the sea, nation of the ruined! The word of the Lord is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines; and I will destroy you so that there is no inhabitant.
verses.2:6: And the strip by the sea will be a resting place for shepherds and folds for flocks;
verses.2:7: and it will be the strip of the one who remains from the house of Judah: there they will pasture, in the houses of Ashkelon they will rest toward evening, for the Lord their God will visit them and turn away their captivity.
verses.2:8: "I have heard the reproach of Moab and the blasphemies of the sons of Ammon, with which they have reproached My people and magnified themselves against their borders.
verses.2:9: Therefore, as I live," says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, "surely Moab will be like Sodom, and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah: a dryness of thorns, and heaps of salt, and a wasteland forever; the remnant of My people will plunder them, and the survivors of My nation will possess them."
verses.2:10: This will happen to them for their pride, because they have blasphemed and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.
verses.2:11: Fearsome is the Lord against them, and He will diminish all the gods of the earth; and men will worship Him, each from his own place, all the islands of the nations.
verses.2:12: "And you too, Ethiopians, will be killed by My sword."
verses.2:13: And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria, and He will turn the beautiful one into a desolation, and into a trackless place, and like a wasteland.
verses.2:14: And flocks will lie down in her midst, all the beasts of the nations; and the pelican and the hedgehog will lodge on her thresholds: the voice of one singing in the window, the raven on the lintel, for I will diminish her strength.
verses.2:15: This is the glorious city dwelling in confidence, which said in her heart, "I am, and besides me there is no other anymore." How has she been turned into a wasteland, a lair of a beast? Everyone who passes by her will hiss and wave his hand.
verses.3:1: Woe to the defiant and redeemed city, the dove!
verses.3:2: She has not listened to the voice, and she has not accepted discipline; she has not trusted in the Lord, she has not drawn near to her God.
verses.3:3: Her princes in her midst are like roaring lions; her judges are wolves in the evening; they left nothing for the morning.
verses.3:4: Her prophets are mad, faithless men; her priests have polluted what is holy; they have acted unjustly against the law.
verses.3:5: The just Lord in her midst will not do iniquity; morning by morning He will bring His judgment to light, and it will not be hidden; but the unjust one has not known shame.
verses.3:6: "I have destroyed nations, and their corners have been demolished; I have made their streets deserted, with no one passing by; their cities have been made desolate, with no man remaining, nor any inhabitant.
verses.3:7: I said, 'Surely you will fear Me; you will accept discipline; and her dwelling will not perish, because of all the things in which I have visited her.' Yet, rising at dawn, they corrupted all their thoughts.
verses.3:8: Therefore wait for Me," says the Lord, "on the day of My resurrection in the future; for My judgment is to gather the nations and assemble the kingdoms, and to pour out upon them My indignation, all the wrath of My fury; for in the fire of My zeal the whole earth will be devoured.
verses.3:9: For then I will restore to the peoples a chosen lip, so that all of them may call upon the name of the Lord and serve Him with one shoulder.
verses.3:10: Beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, from there My suppliants, the sons of My scattered ones, will bring an offering to Me.
verses.3:11: On that day you will not be put to shame over all your contrivances by which you have transgressed against Me, for then I will remove from your midst the boasters of your pride, and you will not exalt yourself anymore on My holy mountain.
verses.3:12: And I will leave in your midst a poor and needy people, and they will hope in the name of the Lord.
verses.3:13: The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity nor speak a lie, and a deceitful tongue will not be found in their mouth; for they themselves will pasture and lie down, and there will be no one to terrify them."
verses.3:14: Give praise, daughter of Zion; shout for joy, Israel; be glad and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.3:15: The Lord has taken away your judgment; He has turned back your enemies. The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst; you will fear evil no more.
verses.3:16: On that day it will be said to Jerusalem, "Do not fear"; to Zion, "Do not let your hands grow weak."
verses.3:17: The Lord your God in your midst is mighty; He Himself will save. He will rejoice over you with gladness; He will be silent in His love; He will exult over you with praise.
verses.3:18: "I will gather the frivolous ones who had departed from the law, because they were from you, so that you will no longer have reproach over them.
verses.3:19: Look, I Myself will kill all who have afflicted you at that time; and I will save the limping one, and I will gather her who had been cast out; and I will make them into praise and into a name in every land of their shame,
verses.3:20: at that time when I bring you in, and at the time when I gather you. For I will make you into a name and into praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes," says the Lord.

notes.1:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom (commonly understood as "utterly sweep away") literally as "Gathering, I will gather" (Congregans congregabo), continuing the participle into verse 3.
notes.1:3: The Vulgate reads "there will be ruins of the wicked" (ruinæ impiorum erunt), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the stumbling blocks along with the wicked."
notes.1:9: The Vulgate specifies "arrogantly steps over the threshold" (arroganter ingreditur, where Hebrew has "leaps over") and identifies the house as "the house of the Lord their God" (where Hebrew has "the house of their master").
notes.1:11: "The Mortar" translates Latin Pila (the Jerusalem market quarter called Maktesh in Hebrew; similarly "the Second" in 1:10 translates Secunda, the Second Quarter of Jerusalem), and "wrapped in silver" (involuti argento) reflects a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Hebrew has "those who weigh out silver."
notes.1:16: Latin angulos ("corners," here and in 3:6) refers to the fortified corner towers or battlements of city walls.
notes.2:2: The Vulgate construes the opening clause as "before the decree brings forth the day that passes like dust," reading pulverem ("dust") where the Hebrew has "chaff."
notes.2:5: "Strip" renders Latin funiculus (literally "cord" or "measuring line," used across 2:5-7 for an allotted tract of land), and "nation of the ruined" (gens perditorum) reflects Jerome's etymological rendering of the Hebrew proper name Cherethites.
notes.2:9: The Vulgate reads "a dryness of thorns" (siccitas spinarum), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a possession of nettles."
notes.2:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew city name Nineveh etymologically as speciosam ("the beautiful one").
notes.2:14: Several Vulgate-distinct readings appear here: "pelican" (onocrotalus) and "hedgehog" (ericius) lodging "on her thresholds" (in liminibus, vs. Hebrew "capitals"), "the raven on the lintel" (corvus, matching the Septuagint vs. Hebrew "desolation"), and the first-person clause "for I will diminish her strength" (vs. Hebrew "for the cedarwork has been laid bare").
notes.3:1: The Vulgate reads "redeemed" (redempta, vs. Hebrew "defiled") and "dove" (columba, vs. Hebrew "oppressing"), reflecting alternate root derivations of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.3:8: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate reads "on the day of My resurrection in the future" (in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for the day when I rise up to prey" (or "as a witness").
notes.3:18: The Vulgate reads "the frivolous ones who had departed from the law" (Nugas, qui a lege recesserant), a distinctive rendering of the Hebrew phrase "those grieving over the appointed feast."
notes.3:20: "Turn back your captivity" (like "turn away their captivity" in 2:7) preserves the Vulgate's literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom often translated "restore your fortunes."
